issues.problem: The patch always searches the query for the CQL-escaped password (' becomes ''). The lexer also accepts pg-style $$...$$ string literals (Lexer.g STRING_LITERAL), where a single quote is written as-is. Trigger: CREATE ROLE r WITH PASSWORD = $$pa'ss$$, or ALTER ROLE with the same form, with auditing enabled. RoleOptions holds pa'ss, the escaped search string is pa''ss, and the query text contains pa'ss. The regex does not match, replaceAll returns the query unchanged, and the plaintext password goes to the audit log and any other consumer of obfuscatePassword. The old code matched this input, so this is a regression for dollar-quoted passwords that contain a single quote. The new tests only build '...'-quoted queries, so they do not catch it.

lenses.name: cassandra-standards
lenses.summary: The patch fixes PasswordObfuscator.obfuscate(String, RoleOptions) by wrapping the password in Pattern.quote(), so regex metacharacters and \E no longer leak the password or throw PatternSyntaxException. It also CQL-escapes single quotes before matching. That matches CASSANDRA-21113 and stays in scope: one source file, a CHANGES.txt entry under 4.0.21, and tests. The change is a bug fix, which is appropriate for the 4.0 release branch. It touches audit-log secret masking, so the security check applies. One risk remains: the new quote-escaping assumes the query used '...' quoting. A password containing a single quote that was written as a $$...$$ literal is raw in the query, so the escaped form no longer matches and the password would be logged in clear text. Before this patch that case matched literally and was obfuscated. The PR does not touch .claude/, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and I found no review-steering text. No NEWS.txt entry is needed, because the change has no user-facing API effect beyond audit-log masking.

findings.rule: security-secret-exposure: audit-log DCL statements must never contain the cleartext password
findings.problem: The new code always searches for the password with ' doubled to ''. CQL also accepts $$...$$ string literals, in which a single quote appears unescaped. For `CREATE ROLE r WITH PASSWORD = $$it's$$`, RoleOptions holds `it's` and the query contains `it's`. The pattern now looks for `it''s`, finds no match, and returns the query unchanged, so the password goes to the audit log in clear text. The old unquoted code matched this case, so the patch introduces a leak that did not exist before for this input. The tests only cover the '...' form. I traced this from the grammar and the code but did not run it, so confidence is medium.
findings.fix: Obfuscate against both forms: replace the quoted raw password and its '-escaped form, for example by building an alternation of Pattern.quote(raw) and Pattern.quote(escaped), longest first. Alternatively, fall back to the prefix-based obfuscate(String) when neither form matches. Add a test using a $$...$$ literal with an embedded single quote.

lenses.name: cass-logic-boundary
lenses.summary: The patch fixes PasswordObfuscator.obfuscate(query, opts). It wraps the password in Pattern.quote() so regex metacharacters and \E no longer break or evade the match. It also CQL-escapes single quotes in the password before matching. It adds tests for \E sequences and for every printable ASCII special character at the start, middle and end of a password. I applied the logic.md and boundary.md checklists from the refdir. I read only the diff and the code it touches; nothing was left unreviewed. The Pattern.quote() change is correct. The replacement string is the constant "$1*******", so the password does not reach the replacement side. I found one regression: the new quote-doubling no longer matches passwords written as $$-quoted CQL string literals.

findings.rule: logic: the matched form must equal the form in the query; the new CQL-escape assumption holds only for '...' literals
findings.problem: The patch assumes the query always holds the password in single-quote-escaped form (' doubled to ''). CQL also accepts $$...$$ string literals, where a single quote is written raw. Trigger: `CREATE ROLE r WITH PASSWORD = $$it's$$` gives RoleOptions password `it's`. The patch searches for the quoted `it''s`, which is not in the query, so replaceAll matches nothing and returns the query unchanged. The cleartext password then goes to the audit log. Before the patch, the raw `it's` pattern matched this form and was obfuscated. So this is a regression for $$-quoted passwords containing a single quote, and it is the leak the ticket sets out to remove. I could not confirm that every caller passes the raw query text, which is why confidence is medium.
findings.fix: Match both forms. Build an alternation of Pattern.quote(raw) and Pattern.quote(raw.replace("'", "''")), longest first or de-duplicated when they are equal. Or fall back to obfuscate(query) when the quoted pattern does not match. Add a test with a $$-quoted password containing a single quote.

findings.rule: logic: failure to match is silently accepted
findings.problem: If the quoted password is not found in the query for any reason, replaceAll returns the original query and the password is logged in cleartext, with no fallback. The new test covers only '...' literals, so it would not catch this. The $$ case in lb-1 is one concrete example.
findings.fix: When the result equals the input and the query contains the password token, fall back to the unconditional obfuscate(query) truncation, which is safe.

lenses.name: cass-test-regime
lenses.summary: CASSANDRA-21113 (4.0): PasswordObfuscator.obfuscate(query, opts) now builds its regex with Pattern.quote() and doubles single quotes in the password before matching. The change is single-node string logic, so unit tests in test/unit are the right suite and no dtest or upgrade test is needed. The new tests are testPasswordWithRegexEndQuote and an exhaustive printable-ASCII loop in testAllPrintableSpecialCharactersObfuscation. The ticket's pre-fix output shows both fail without the fix (leaks for $ + ? * ^, PatternSyntaxException for ( ) [ \ {, wrong output for |). The tests are deterministic with no sleeps, timeouts or shared state, so repeated runs are not needed. Checklist applied: cassandra-injvm-dtest/SKILL.md, which is not applicable to this unit-level change. I also used testing.md. Not reviewed: nothing. Gaps: no test passes the password as a $$-quoted string literal, and no test goes through the Create/AlterRoleStatement.obfuscatePassword callers.
